key_insight: lPINN moves most of the neural-network learning offline by pretraining a frozen nonlinear basis, then solves new PDE instances online with only a final linear fit constrained by physics.
engineering_relevance: This can cut inference time dramatically while improving accuracy for forward and inverse differential-equation problems, making PINN-style solvers more practical for repeated simulation and parameter estimation.
method: Pretrain continuous neural basis functions from an ensemble of numerical solutions using derivative data or physics residuals.
Freeze the hidden layers and solve each new instance by minimizing PDE residuals plus initial/boundary/regularization/observation terms.
Keep the learned representation differentiable so it can be evaluated on finer meshes without retraining.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tests on advection-diffusion, Burgers', and nonlinear pendulum problems, with lower solution/parameter errors than vanilla PINNs and online speedups from about 10x to over 1000x, especially when residual or measurement data are scarce.
watch_item: The offline basis must be trained on representative solution ensembles; performance may drop if new problems differ significantly from the pretraining distribution.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
